evidence: The PR deletes the kch42/buzhash entry from policy.json, leaving only fslock, while FORKS.md still said policy.json 'still carries two reviewed exceptions'; a0cac46 changes it to 'a reviewed exception (fslock's)'.
guidance_note: When deleting an entry from a list, grep the repo for prose that counts that list ('two exceptions', 'both current exceptions') and update every count in the same commit.

evidence: The suggested `go mod tidy` was wrong: the agent showed the h1: row is required by the dolt fork's binlogreplication test graph. But the reviewer's other branch, 'the changelog claim is wrong and should be corrected', was right. The bullet says 'in any module, at build time or test time' and the scoping existed only in the agent's reply. The same claim came back as F9, which the agent accepted with exactly that disclosure.
guidance_note: When rejecting a reviewer's proposed fix, check whether the facts in your rebuttal contradict the text under review; if your reply has to narrow a claim, move that narrowing into the text instead of leaving it in the thread.

evidence: There was no real count contradiction: each bullet recorded its own contemporaneous delta, and the golang-lru removal did take MPL to zero. Read top-down, though, the release notes did seem to contradict each other. a0cac46 adds 'the remaining two were the golang-lru coordinates, whose removal (recorded above) later took it to zero'.
guidance_note: When a changelog stacks bullets that each state a running count, write every count with its point in time ('on the then-current master', 'later took it to N') so the bullets read correctly in any order.

evidence: Both stale counts were real: FORKS.md 'two reviewed exceptions' and graph_report.go 'Both current exceptions'. a0cac46 fixed both, and made the graph_report comment count-free ('Every current exception covers a module...') so later exception removals cannot make it stale again.
guidance_note: When deleting an entry from a list, grep the repo for prose that counts that list and replace the counts with count-free wording.

evidence: The changelog repeated FORKS.md patch 3's 200k-tuple and 2,257-chunk evidence, and its 56,933-chunk figure appeared nowhere in FORKS.md. a0cac46 moves both verification legs into FORKS.md and replaces the changelog's evidence with a pointer. One-source-of-truth applies because two documents held the same facts.
guidance_note: Write verification evidence only in the document that owns the patch, and have the changelog point to it instead of repeating numbers.

evidence: The reviewer's 153 total is wrong. The agent shows the mysql removal merged before the 156 baseline: 'its step is inside the 155'. The misreading is real, though. F3's fix in a0cac46 put the MPL count in chronological order but left the component count (156→155, 155→154) undated, so the bullets still did not show which removal came first. 445cb45 adds the ordering parenthetical.
guidance_note: When fixing a chronology misread between changelog bullets, check every count the bullets share (MPL count and component count) and date all of them in the same fix.

evidence: The reviewer names the cause: 'the same chronology defect the 3→2 MPL wording on the mysql bullet just fixed'. The golang-lru bullet's '155 components' was still undated next to the buzhash bullet's 155→154. a0cac46 fixed only the MPL count, and 445cb45 dates the 155.
guidance_note: When fixing a chronology misread between changelog bullets, check every count the bullets share (MPL count and component count) and date all of them in the same fix.

evidence: False-positive flag: 445cb45 changed only the count parenthetical. The clause 'the same residue class as the freetype entry' appears unchanged in the pre-review diff hunks. The claim was wrong: freetype has a full h1: source hash and ships GPL text at licenses/gpl.txt. 6be23e3 rewords it to the same ticket but a different residue class.
guidance_note: Before writing that one item is 'the same class' as another, check the second item against the same criteria (h1: source hash or /go.mod-only, ships text or not).

evidence: False-positive flag: 445cb45 did not touch the mysql bullet's 'in any module' sentence. This finding is F2 raised again after the agent declined it, not something a fix introduced. The agent concedes 'the scoping lived in my reply, not in the text', and 6be23e3 adds the go.sum/test-graph residue disclosure.
guidance_note: When a pushback depends on scoping a claim more narrowly than the text states it, edit the text in the same round; a declined finding whose premise was true comes back as a new review round.

narrative: This PR removes buzhash and updates counts in FORKS.md, graph_report.go and CHANGELOG. In round 0 the agent fixed the stale exception counts well and moved duplicated evidence into FORKS.md. F3's chronology fix covered only the MPL count, so round 1 found the same misread in the component count (F6, F7). F2's go-sql-driver overclaim was declined with a correct rebuttal of the reviewer's tidy suggestion, but the text kept overclaiming and the finding returned as F9 in round 2. F8 was a pre-existing wrong comparison that the review reached late.
guidance_observations: The agent's F2 pushback was factually right about go.sum but did not answer the reviewer's other branch, that the text overclaims; when a finding offers two branches, answer both.
The changelog bullets are long and each carries running counts; any edit to one bullet's numbers needs every sibling bullet's numbers re-read in the same pass.

evidence: The new package doc said contention is 'stamped with a domain sentinel', but Acquire's own doc names 'a collector's silent skip' as a valid meaning. The agent added a third shape the reviewer missed, the mirror's coalesce. 2f2ef36 rewords to 'given its domain meaning ... a store sentinel, a collector's deliberate silent skip, a mirror's coalesce'.
guidance_note: When writing a rule that summarizes how callers handle a value, list the actual callers (grep `acquired` consumers) and check that the rule covers each one before declaring it.

evidence: The reviewer cites store.go:281 ensureDoltDatabase, which runs CREATE DATABASE and branch SQL before withCommitLock at :291, so 'Store.Open's first SQL use is migrate' was false. The agent confirmed this and narrowed the claim to the long-lived engine. That narrowing over-generalized: F8 shows it also matched OpenSync.
guidance_note: Before writing 'X's first use is Y', trace X's call path from the entry point and list each SQL call in order; do not infer it from the one call site you were looking at.

evidence: The changelog repeated the package doc's false 'Store.Open's first SQL use is migrate' claim, with the same ensureDoltDatabase ordering problem. 2f2ef36 applies the same narrowing to the changelog.
guidance_note: When a changelog summarizes a doc, write the doc first, verify it, and then derive the summary, so one wrong claim does not ship twice.

evidence: This duplicates F1 and names the second non-sentinel consumer: sync_bg.go:160-164 returns nil on contention, a silent coalesce. 2f2ef36's reword names coalesce explicitly.
guidance_note: When writing a rule that summarizes how callers handle a value, list the actual callers and check that the rule covers each one before declaring it.

evidence: 'a lock never waited on cannot hold-and-wait' was wrong: mirrorCycle holds sync-push across OpenSync, which blocks on the workspace and engine locks. The agent restated the correct reason: 'no inbound wait-edge cannot complete a cycle'. 2f2ef36 places sync-push as outermost in practice. The fix updated only the package doc, which led to F11.
guidance_note: Justify a deadlock-freedom claim by edges, saying who waits on whom, and trace what a lock's holder goes on to acquire before calling the lock order-free.

evidence: retryTransientGCContention calls s.reconnect while withCommitLock is held (commit_lock.go:152/:176). The rotated engine therefore re-acquires LOCK under commit, so 'One deviation exists today' was not exhaustive. 2f2ef36 names both acquisitions.
guidance_note: Before writing 'one deviation exists', grep every place the resource is acquired (every engine open or reconnect), not only the first.

evidence: The changelog said 'owner exclusion is an flock through filelock.Acquire', but commit_lock.go still uses O_EXCL with PID/mtime staleness, and the package doc names that as a predating mechanism. 2f2ef36 adds the 'declared rule, not yet a universal fact' caveat with il18.2/.4.
guidance_note: When a changelog summarizes a doc that states a rule along with its known exceptions, carry the exceptions into the summary, or it will state the rule as already true.

evidence: The round-0 text named only 'Store.Open's first SQL use'. 2f2ef36 generalized it to 'the long-lived Store engine ... its first SQL use is migrate', which now also covers OpenSync, whose first SQL is SyncListRemotes outside any commit lock. The agent verified this and 6dfcd2b narrows the claim back to Store.Open.
guidance_note: When narrowing a claim in response to a finding, list every constructor that produces the subject you are now naming (Open, OpenSync, OpenForRead) and check the new claim against each.

evidence: False-positive flag: 'every write-engine open is already serialized by the engine lock before commit is reached' is byte-identical to the round-0 text; 2f2ef36 only re-wrapped it. The reviewer cites adopt.go:360 cloneRemoteDatabase opening engineWrite under only LockWorkspaceExclusive, and the agent verified it.
guidance_note: Before writing 'every X is serialized by Y', grep every opener of X (openDoltPool with engineWrite) and confirm that each one takes Y.

evidence: False-positive flag: the 'a reservation nobody holds across a window (the snapshot slot's os.Mkdir...)' parenthetical is unchanged from round 0. Take holds .reserve through `defer os.Remove` for the whole copy window (snapshot.go:149-153), so 'nobody holds' was false. 6dfcd2b separates the trace file from the beacon-proven slot.
guidance_note: When you classify each example in a doc's parenthetical, read each example's code for how long it holds the resource before grouping them under one property.

evidence: 2f2ef36 rewrote the package doc to call sync-push 'outermost in practice', but the changelog in the same commit still lists workspace as the outermost lock with no sync-push caveat. 6dfcd2b adds the caveat inline.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a doc that a changelog entry summarizes, re-diff the summary against the changed doc in the same commit.

evidence: False-positive flag: the flagged line (filelock.go:23, the 'one home' header) dates from the original PR, and commit_lock.go's header ('exactly one lock type ... cannot deadlock') was never touched. The original PR claimed to be the one home but did not sweep the competing deadlock story, a gap the agent concedes is 'exactly the second-map contradiction the ticket exists to eliminate'.
guidance_note: When declaring a doc the single home of a rule, grep for every other comment that states the same rule (here 'deadlock', 'lock type', 'lock order') and make each one defer to the home in the same PR.

evidence: False-positive flag: the 'two placement exceptions (... the adopt-pending marker inside the dolt root)' wording is in the original round-0 changelog. By listing the marker as an exception to 'lock files sit beside', the changelog implies it is a lock, while the package doc calls it 'a condemnation record, not a lock'.
guidance_note: When a changelog summarizes a doc, carry the doc's qualifiers ('not a lock') along with the facts they qualify.

evidence: False-positive flag: 'inverts the order against every live Store' is in the round-0 text of both the changelog and the package doc. The same doc says 'read engines never wait on LOCK', so only write Stores are at risk. The agent fixed both places in 6dfcd2b.
guidance_note: Check each 'every X' in a new invariant doc against the subtypes of X that the same doc already excludes.

narrative: This is a docs-only PR declaring the lock discipline. Every reviewer claim checked out against the cited code, and the agent accepted all 14 with code-anchored plans. Of round 1's seven findings, two were caused by round-0 fixes: F8 (the long-lived-engine narrowing over-generalized to OpenSync) and F11 (the sync-push placement updated in the doc but not the changelog). The other five were pre-existing overclaims the first pass missed. Round 1 would have run anyway because of those five, and round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The PR wrote an invariant doc full of universal claims ('every write-engine open', 'one deviation', 'nobody holds', 'every live Store') without tracing each one through the code. Twelve of 14 findings were universals that a grep for the subject's producers would have falsified.
The doc and the changelog were edited separately in each fix, so changelog drift kept recurring; regenerate or re-diff the changelog summary from the doc after every doc edit.
